Study

What 230 UK businesses paying for Google Ads actually measure, sector by sector

Of 230 UK businesses with live Google Ads in 15 service sectors, 43% show a Google Ads conversion tag on their site, 21% count visits with Google Analytics and show no Google Ads tag at all, and 14% show no measurement of any kind. Four in five publish a clickable phone number, and just over half of those have nothing in place to count the call. These companies are paying for clicks today. A large share cannot tell which click became a customer.

The short version

43%show a Google Ads conversion tag on the home page or inside the tag container
21%count visits with Google Analytics and show no Google Ads tag at all
14%show no measurement of any kind
53%of the sites with a clickable phone number have nothing we could find to count the call

All 230 businesses had a Google ad shown in the United Kingdom between 23 October and 13 November 2026, according to Google's own Ads Transparency Center, and all of them are marked there as verified advertisers. They are paying for clicks now. Fewer than half show Google which click became a customer.

The figures are free to quote with a link to this page. The table by sector can be downloaded as a CSV file.

Six groups, adding up to 100%

Every site falls into exactly one group, read from the outside, with no access to anyone's account.

A Google Ads conversion tag is visible43%Google Ads is being told about at least one kind of result. Whether it is the right result is a separate question.

Other tags only6%An empty Tag Manager container, a retired Universal Analytics tag, a Meta Pixel or a heatmap tool, with nothing for Google Ads.

No measurement of any kind14%No Tag Manager, no Google tag, no Analytics, no Meta Pixel. The adverts run and nothing on the site records what they bring.

The phone call is the lead, and half the time nothing counts it

80% of the sites publish a phone number a visitor can tap. For most of these businesses the call is the enquiry they want. Among the 185 sites with a clickable number:

  • 18% carry Google's own website call conversion, which swaps the number on the page for a Google forwarding number.
  • 5% carry a call tracking service from another supplier.
  • 37% have a tag that fires when the number is clicked, which counts taps and not conversations.
  • 53% have none of the three.

One caveat matters here. Google's help page on conversion measurement says "Some kinds of conversion measurement don't require a tag", and gives the example of calls from call assets, where "you use a Google forwarding number to track when the call came from one of your ads". A business can therefore count calls made straight from the advert with nothing on its site. What it cannot count that way is the visitor who clicks the advert, reads the page and then rings the number on it.

What this means if you are paying for Google Ads

  • Ask one question of whoever runs your account. Which conversion action is the primary one, and when did it last record a conversion. If the answer takes more than a minute, read what to check when conversions are not tracking.
  • A phone number on the page is not a measured phone call. 80% of these sites show a number and 53% of those have nothing to count the call that follows the click.
  • Analytics is not conversion tracking. Google Analytics tells you people came. Only a conversion sent to Google Ads, or imported into it, tells the bidding which clicks were worth paying for.
  • Consent handling is part of measurement. A banner that blocks tags with no consent mode behind it removes a share of your conversions from the reports. Google explains how consent mode recovers part of them.
  • If your site is in the last group, the first job is not a new campaign. It is a tag, a conversion action and a test. That is what a conversion tracking setup covers, and a PPC audit will tell you which group your own site is in.

How this was measured

  1. Finding the advertisers. On 13 November 2026 we searched Google's Ads Transparency Center, with the region set to the United Kingdom, for the words a business in each of 15 service sectors is likely to have in its web address, such as plumbers, solicitors, dental or removals, alone and combined with London, Manchester, Birmingham, Leeds and Bristol. The Transparency Center returns advertiser websites that match.
  2. Keeping only live advertisers. We checked 420 of those websites in the Transparency Center and kept the 301 with an advert last shown in the UK on or after 14 October 2026.
  3. Reading the sites. We read the source of each home page, every Google Tag Manager container and Google tag file it refers to, and, for sites built on Wix, the list of tags the platform loads. 277 home pages could be read. The rest refused the request or did not answer.
  4. Removing what did not belong. We removed sites that were not UK businesses, were not in the sector they were found under, or were parked pages. 230 sites remain.
  5. Counting. Each share on this page is a count over those 230 sites, or over the sites of one sector. Nothing was estimated or weighted.

What this study cannot see

  • Tags on other pages. Only the home page was read. A conversion tag placed only on a thank-you page is missed, which is why sites with a Google Ads tag and no visible conversion are reported as their own group.
  • Imports from Analytics. A business can import results from Google Analytics into Google Ads with no Google Ads tag on the site. That is invisible from outside, so the analytics-only group is not described as untracked.
  • Calls counted inside the advert. Calls made straight from a call asset need no tag on the site.
  • Tags loaded by a script. The pages were read without running their scripts and without accepting cookies. Where a page showed signs of a tag whose ID we could not read, it was counted in a separate group.
  • The sample is not random. Looking for trade words in web addresses favours smaller local firms whose address names what they do. Large national brands are mostly absent.
  • Small groups. Sectors hold between 7 and 20 sites, and the reading was taken on a single day.

An earlier edition of this page, published on 6 November 2026, covered 34 sites. This edition replaces it. The larger sample and the reading of Google tag files and Wix tag lists explain the differences between the two.

Questions people ask before hiring

How many UK businesses advertising on Google have conversion tracking?

Of the 230 UK advertisers read for this study, 43% show a Google Ads conversion tag on the home page or inside their tag container. A further 13% carry a Google Ads tag with no conversion action visible from the home page, and 14% show no measurement of any kind.

Does a Google Analytics tag count as Google Ads conversion tracking?

No. Google Analytics counts visits and events. Google Ads only learns which click became an enquiry when a conversion action is set up in Google Ads or imported from Analytics. In this study 21% of sites had Analytics or a Google tag and no Google Ads tag at all.

Which UK sectors measure their Google Ads best?

Among the 15 sectors read, mortgage and financial advice had the highest share of sites with a Google Ads conversion tag, at 69%, and cleaning the lowest, at 12%. The groups are small, so the order should be read as a picture and not as a ranking.

How did you find the advertisers?

Through Google's Ads Transparency Center, with the region set to the United Kingdom. We searched for trade words that appear in web addresses, kept the websites with an advert last shown in the UK in the previous 30 days, and removed those that were not UK businesses in the sector. All 230 are marked as verified advertisers.

Can a business count phone calls with no tag on its site?

Partly. Google's help page says some conversion measurement does not require a tag, and gives calls from call assets as the example. That counts calls made straight from the advert. It does not count the visitor who clicks through, reads the page and rings the number on it, which needs a call conversion or a call tracking service on the site.

What should I do if my site has no tag?

Ask whoever runs the account to show you the Conversions page in Google Ads and the status of each action. If there is no action, or it is inactive, the tag needs to be installed and tested before any bidding strategy can work.
